top.line: Why a static website cell edited by Claude is an alternative to WordPress, Wix and Squarespace.
top.para: Reach, attack surface, complexity, lock-in, a converter.

in-short.line: The market is platform sites; rich and complex; 11,334 vulnerabilities; lock-in; static; Claude; a converter.

market.line: WordPress on 38.5% of websites; Wix 6.11 million paying subscriptions; Squarespace over 5.2 million.

complex.line: 60% of WordPress sites use a page builder; 45% pass Core Web Vitals; a third run an older version.
complex.para: A banner that would not change.

attack.line: 11,334 WordPress vulnerabilities in 2025, 91% in plugins, 46% unfixed at disclosure, five hours to exploitation.

lockin.line: Wix sites cannot leave Wix; Squarespace exports part of a site; both raised prices in 2026.
lockin.para: The price is what the platform says.

static.line: Static files, no database, no plugins, no cookies by default, in the owner's repository, edited by Claude.

foot.line: Owners can still make mistakes: policies, CI, a leak scan and a security agent, and partners' services.

converter.line: WordPress exports everything and Squarespace exports in its format: one converter for both.

opportunity.line: A tiny share is enough: one in ten thousand of Wix's subscriptions is over 600 sites.
opportunity.para: Own it, pay once, talk to Claude.

limits.line: Vendor security figures; no static-site study; site counts unknown; converter a proposal.

sources.line: W3Techs, Wix, Web Almanac, WordPress.org, Patchstack, Wordfence, Sucuri and others.
